system.name: Simbricks
system.one_liner: a general full-stack simulation framework (in the style of Simbricks) combining a host simulator (gem5) with accelerator simulators over a simulated interconnect

components.name: Application 1
components.role: an unmodified application running on top of the simulated OS

components.name: Application 2
components.role: another unmodified application running on top of the simulated OS

components.name: Operating System
components.role: the unmodified OS that, with the applications, runs natively inside gem5's simulated CPU

components.name: gem5
components.role: cycle-accurate system simulator that models the host CPU, cache, memory, and device interfaces

components.name: CPU Simulator
components.role: simulates the host CPU with cycle-level fidelity

components.name: Devices
components.role: grouping of simulated device interfaces exposed by gem5, including the Accelerator Adapter

components.name: Accelerator Adapter
components.role: gem5-side device model that exposes the accelerator to the simulated host over MMIO and DMA

components.name: Memory Simulator
components.role: simulates the host's main memory, target of accelerator DMA

components.name: Interconnect Simulator
components.role: simulates the interconnect (e.g., PCIe) linking the host simulator to the accelerator simulators

components.name: Accelerator Simulators
components.role: grouping of alternative accelerator-simulation approaches (RTL or a custom Model)

components.name: Model
components.role: a custom, presumably higher-level model of the accelerator

content.key_idea: The figure shows a Simbricks-style full-stack simulator where gem5 cycle-accurately simulates the host (CPU, cache, memory, and a device adapter) while separate RTL or custom-model simulators model accelerators, connected through a simulated interconnect via MMIO and DMA interfaces.
content.reading_order: Top-down then left-right: applications/OS sit above gem5 (CPU/cache/memory/device simulators), which connects rightward through the Interconnect Simulator to the RTL/Model accelerator simulators.

summary: This figure gives background, not the paper's own contribution: a simplified, Simbricks-style full-stack simulation framework for hardware-accelerated software stacks. A tan box holds the unmodified software stack (Application 1, Application 2, and the Operating System); it runs inside the blue gem5 box below, which cycle-accurately simulates the host system via a CPU Simulator, a Cache/Memory Simulator pair, and a Devices group containing an Accelerator Adapter. The CPU Simulator and Accelerator Adapter exchange MMIO Read/Write, and the adapter exchanges DMA traffic with the Memory Simulator. To the right, a vertical Interconnect Simulator box (representing simulated PCIe, among other placements) links the Accelerator Adapter to a separate pink Accelerator Simulators zone, where either an RTL simulator or a custom Model simulates the accelerator itself.
summary_zh: 图1为背景框架：软件栈(App1/2+OS)运行于gem5之上，gem5含CPU/缓存/内存模拟器与Accelerator Adapter，经MMIO/DMA交互；右侧经Interconnect连接RTL/Model加速器模拟器。
notes: This figure depicts prior-art/background (a Simbricks-style baseline using gem5) per its own caption, not the paper's novel NEX/DSim design, which the text says later replaces the gem5 component shown here (in a subsequent figure not included in this batch); all components are therefore marked novel:false.
